angle: A mono-green deck that never taps out: Radagast's discount-and-flash resets on every player's turn, so untapped Forests become a standing tax on the whole table, traps teach three opponents not to attack, and the kill is counted rather than hoped — five bodies, then Craterhoof cast at home in your own main, because the flashy end-step Hoof is verified to kill nobody.

teases: Green wipes the sky: a {3}{G} Hydra eats every flier at instant speed
A 1/1 kills a 6/6 and draws two cards — the Frostfang trap, on the record
36 is not 40: the Craterhoof arithmetic, counted to the point
Their wrath, your four cards: Fecundity pays the wake

departments.note: Full-bleed Anna Podedworna commander art; issue.json tagline 'Every turn is your turn.' is the thesis in five words. The kicker states stack 001's finding (the window resets on every player's turn — four a round), the dominant coverline states stack 005's holding (flash the Hoof to dodge, cast him at home to kill). Both violators are literally true: seven checker-passed case files, and a 10,000-iteration goldfish at seed 42.
Renderer-standard Flight Plan: five acts, promises verbatim from issue_spec, tier legend and masthead trio printed in full.

departments.headline: FOUR TURNS, FOUR WINDOWS
departments.dek: You never have to draw him, and that is the whole argument. Radagast is guaranteed access to a rules engine — a discount and a flash window that reset on every player's turn — and the whole 99 is built on that guarantee.
departments.body:
Exhibit one: the text. The first creature spell you cast each turn costs {2} less and can be cast as though it had flash. The load-bearing words are 'each turn' — the printed template 'each of your turns' exists, and Radagast does not use it. A turn is a structural unit every player takes (CR 500.1), so the count zeroes at every untap, yours and theirs alike: four windows per round in a four-player pod. One candour the record keeps: no single rule states that an each-turn count resets. The holding is derived from the ability's text plus the definition of a turn, and the checker judged the derivation sound exactly as hedged (stack 001).

Now the zone. Your commander begins the game in the command zone and is the only card you always have (CR 903.4). That matters doubly for a deck that is a posture rather than a pile — you cannot hold mana open around an engine you might never draw. The goldfish puts him on the field on a mean turn 4.0, and by turn six in 94.1% of runs. Every other card here assumes he is there; the format is what makes that assumption legal.

The tax, on the record: {2}{G}{G} the first time, and each recast from the zone costs {2} more (CR 903.8). Four, then six, then eight. Six is affordable in a deck whose mana is 36 Forests and nine creature producers. Eight is a lost round of windows.

Coach's ledger on that: insure, don't re-buy. Nine protection copies are the premium on a commander-gated posture — Guardian Augmenter flashes in mid-removal-spell and leaves a hexproof 4/7 where the target used to be, and Tyvar's Stand protects him for one mana at X=0. Yeva, Nature's Herald is insurance of a different kind: a second flash enabler, so answering Radagast no longer switches the whole posture off. The recast is the fallback plan; the insurance is the plan.

Colour identity: mono-green, one line of pips, 63 spells that all agree. What it locks out is just as legible — zero counterspells, and the deck's one board wipe reads only the sky (Whiptongue Hydra eats fliers, nothing else). Veil of Summer is the closest thing to 'no' the deck sells; everything else answers permanents, not spells.

Is the 21-damage clock a plan (CR 903.10a)? A coincidence. He is a 2/5 — eleven clean connections. Your clock is X=6 trample.

The political read is the department's last word. The table sees a four-mana 2/5 Wizard and 36 Forests: fair stompy, zero combos, zero Game Changers, computed floor 1. Let them keep believing it. After he resolves, the true text of this deck is two untapped Forests and a pass.

captions.Radagast of Rhosgobel: **THE METRONOME:** the first creature spell each turn — every turn, all four of them — costs {2} less and casts at instant speed. A round where you only act on your own turn wasted three windows (stack 001).

pilot_tips.text: Budget the recast before you need it: re-buy Radagast only when six mana still leaves {G}{G} open, and spend the insurance suite first — a flashed Guardian Augmenter is two mana cheaper than the tax.

departments.pull_quote: The command zone hands you the engine every game. The 99's only job is to keep it running.

departments.headline: NEVER TAP OUT
departments.dek: Turn four, six Forests open, and the table has already filed you under ramp. Every untapped Forest is a loaded question — and the answer, four times a round, is a discounted body nobody voted for.

captions.Wood Elves: **THE POSTER CARD:** one green mana on an opponent's end step, and the fetched Forest enters untapped — body, land, window, one card (stack 001).
captions.Ohran Frostfang: **THE REPUTATION:** flashed after blockers are declared, everything you lined up turns lethal. Show it once, and two open Forests do the job forever after (stack 002).
captions.Craterhoof Behemoth: **THE APPOINTMENT:** the kill is counted, not hoped for — five bodies on board, then his own precombat main. The end step is for bodies, never for him (stacks 003, 005).
captions.Yeva, Nature's Herald: **THE DOOR:** while she's out, every green creature spell you cast has flash — Radagast's once-a-turn clause binds only the discount, and the second, third, and fourth body of a turn can all arrive on someone else's end step.

pilot_tips.text: Exile Elvish Spirit Guide from a hand the table priced at zero — the trap that fires through an empty-looking board is the one that ends someone's attack phase for the night.

departments.pull_quote: Pass with mana open. This deck plays its best Magic on turns that belong to other people.

departments.headline: SEVENTY SEATS, ONE CLOCK
departments.dek: Seventy seats, every one auditioned against the same clock. Count how many of these lines end with a flash window and how few end with 'tap out' — the roster is the plan, sorted.

roster.role: The gas — draw keyed to what the deck does anyway
The width — the count to five
The dork hump — eight one-mana-class accelerants
The land ramp — the drop that keeps hitting
The aura ramp — the floor the sim can't see
The removal — answers off the creature plan
The toolbox — two wishes and the receipts
cards: Bala Ged Recovery // Bala Ged Sanctuary

captions.Toski, Bearer of Secrets: **THE CONSTANT:** can't be countered, can't be destroyed, must attack — and pays a card every time anyone on your team connects. He shrugged off six damage in stack 002 and skipped the wrath in stack 004.
captions.Scute Swarm: **THE FIFTH BODY:** every land drop is a body, and past six lands every land drop is two. Stack 003 says the fifth body is the entire difference between 36 and lethal.
captions.Whiptongue Hydra: **THE SKY WIPE:** he enters, every flier dies, and he grows a +1/+1 counter per corpse — six mana at retail, {3}{G} at instant speed in a Radagast window. Hold him until the air force commits.

pilot_tips.text: Loop Fauna Shaman toward Craterhoof Behemoth when the count says pivot and toward Caustic Caterpillar when it says stop — with 35 creatures, the spare body in hand is never the card you actually need.

departments.note: Renderer draws per-card prose from manual_prose.card_roles. Groups are ranked load-bearing-first: the traps are the identity, so they lead; the lands close. The commander's entry lives in The Command Zone.

departments.headline: TWO LANDS AND A DORK
departments.dek: 81.5% of first sevens are keeps, so the skill here is not courage — it's recognising the three shapes you still ship. Cover the verdicts and commit.

hands.why: Two lands and an accelerant is the keep shape — kept hands cluster at two to four lands, and turn-one Elves is turn-three Radagast in about a third of games. Frostfang is the trap you hold, Cultivate patches the land drops, and Harmonize is gas that asks for no board. Draw-go from turn three: keep.

Two or more five-plus drops is a stated ship shape — the finishers are the payoff, not the plan, and a finisher is already in hand by turn six in 42.4% of games without you hoarding two of them on turn zero. Three real lands cannot carry a hand whose first meaningful play is turn five.

Three lands, an untapped-Forest accelerant, an engine, and something to do at instant speed. This hand passes with mana open from turn two and never has to tap out to develop — the exact posture the deck is built to hold.

All lands and dorks with nothing to hold up. The mana is perfect and the deck it belongs to is missing — no trap, no engine, no draw. The 81.5% keep rate is earned by hands that do something with the mana, and this one does nothing at any speed.

pilot_tips.text: Never keep a hand because Selvala, Heart of the Wilds is in it — she is a class of one, drawn in 16.3% of games, so she is a bonus, never a reason.

departments.pull_quote: A hand that plays draw-go from turn three is a keep. A hand that must tap out every turn is playing someone else's deck.

departments.headline: TWO BOARDS, TWO COUNTS
departments.dek: Two live boards straight from the record: seven mana with a telegraphed wrath across the table, and a four-body board with the Behemoth in hand. Commit to your line before the Coach shows his.
departments.note: Both recommendations resolve toward patience — 001 to holding all seven at flash speed, 002 to waiting one round on four bodies — so no tip, caption, or pull quote in this section may praise holding mana, counting to five, or the flash windows. The branches must carry the question or the spread stops being one.

departments.headline: THE HOOF STAYS HOME
departments.dek: Everyone at your table has heard the cute line: flash Craterhoof Behemoth on the end step before yours. The record says legal, resolves, survives — and kills nobody. Here is the kill that actually cashes, counted to the point.

callouts.title: COUNT TO FIVE
callouts.text: Stack 003 did the arithmetic with a checker watching. Craterhoof over four bodies reads X=5 — he counts himself — and 7+6+6+7+10 is 36 unblocked into one seat. From 40, the seat survives at 4. The holding is negative and it is the whole department: not lethal.

callouts.title: THE FIFTH BODY WORKS NIGHTS
callouts.text: The window that finds body five costs one green mana: the discount and flash reset on every player's turn (stack 001), and a creature flashed on the end step before yours passes CR 302.6's since-your-turn-began test. It attacks at dawn, no haste required (stack 006).

callouts.title: THE TEMPTATION
callouts.text: Flashing the Hoof into that same end step is legal in every particular — Castle Garenbrig's six restricted green pays a creature spell mid-cast — and the +X/+X ends at that turn's cleanup (CR 514.2). Next morning he swings for 10 unpumped. Legal, resolved, survived: kills nobody (stack 005).

callouts.title: CAST HIM AT HOME
callouts.text: Same mana, your own precombat main: X counts six, his own haste carries the fresh Behemoth into combat, and 40 trample damage is exactly lethal to one 40-life seat (stack 005). Per seat, never the pod — pick your second target before you tap for the first.

callouts.title: IF THE WRATH COMES
callouts.text: The failure case is priced. Under a wrath, Fecundity pays out on every seat's dead — four cards to you in the walked case, one to the wrath's own caster — Toski skips the funeral outright, and Radagast's death is seen before he moves to the command zone (stack 004). The rebuild starts on their end step.

captions.Craterhoof Behemoth: **THE ARITHMETIC:** over four bodies, X=5 deals 36 and a 40-life seat survives at 4. Over five, X=6 deals exactly 40 (stacks 003, 005). The count is the trigger.
captions.Sakura-Tribe Elder: **THE NIGHT SHIFT:** flashed for one green mana on the end step before yours, he wakes attack-ready — both prongs of CR 302.6, on the record (stack 006).
captions.Fecundity: **THE PARACHUTE:** if the pivot meets a wrath, the wrath itself refills your hand — a card per dead creature, anyone's (stack 004).

pilot_tips.text: Hold Heroic Intervention for the turn you commit the board, not the turn it merely saves a body — the pivot happens once, and it is the vote you are calling.

departments.pull_quote: Flash the Hoof to dodge. Cast him at home to kill.
departments.note: Three feature spreads: stack 003 (the count), stack 006 (the dawn attack), stack 005 (the refutation — run it loudest, both halves). Stacks 001 and 004 support as the window and the parachute; stack 002 is the identity's trap and features in The Game Plan and Table Manners instead. Dossier pointers to Judge's Desk cases A-001 through A-007 are renderer-standard.

stat_slab.label: Damage. They start at 40.
stat_slab.note: Craterhoof over four other bodies is 36 unblocked into one seat — loud, board-committing, and short. The fifth body is what clears the bar, so the count is the trigger, not the card.

departments.headline: PAPER CAMOUFLAGE
departments.dek: The table reads you as the fair ramp deck — zero combos, zero Game Changers, a computed floor of 1 — and the paper agrees with them. How long can you afford to keep the paper accurate?

callouts.title: THREAT WINDOW
callouts.text: Three tells flip you from ignored to archenemy, and you control all three: a fifth body, because everyone can count to Craterhoof; visibly hoarded big mana over a wide board, because eleven up is an announcement; and Selvala drawing the table's eye. The count is the trigger — five bodies plus a finisher in hand — so do not start acting like the threat on turn five when the sim says your fifth body arrives nearer turn eight.

captions.Hornet Nest: **THE MINEFIELD:** a 0/2 nobody sane touches — every point of damage it takes becomes that many 1/1 flying deathtouch blockers. Deterrence that works while you spend your mana elsewhere.
captions.Ohran Frostfang: **THE LAWN SIGN:** a player who loses two attackers to open mana stops attacking you for the night. You are not buying creatures — you are buying a reputation (stack 002).

pilot_tips.text: Send Toski at the open seat every turn — the must-attack clause is your alibi, the card is your fee, and nobody at the table blames a squirrel.

departments.pull_quote: Every turn you look like the ramp deck running slightly behind, someone else eats the removal.

departments.headline: ONE HYDRA HOLDS THE SKY
departments.dek: Five archetypes, graded honestly — including a sky the ground plan cannot block, where one flashed Hydra does all the wiping. Zero games played: these are the frames the artifacts support, and the pod will grade them.

threats.read: The flier deck reads your 36 Forests and books the win — green cannot touch the sky, everyone knows it. Let them keep believing it: Whiptongue Hydra destroys every flier on the battlefield when he enters and grows a counter per corpse, and through Radagast's window he is a {3}{G} instant-speed air wipe. The coaching is patience — do not fire him at two birds; let the sky overextend, flash him in after they commit, and collect the whole board. He is one card, so until he turns up the fort holds itself: Hornet Queen's five deathtouch fliers make every swing a losing trade, Arasta and Dawn's Light Archer block at reach, and Warg Tactics kills the one flier that must die right now. Keep your own clock on the ground with Toski and Frostfang, and make the sky player explain why attacking you cost them their air force.

You are the beatdown, full stop — zero counterspells means you lose every long game against inevitability. The toolkit is short and creature-shaped: flash Collector Ouphe through the window on the combo player's own turn, hold Veil of Summer for the turn they answer him, and let Deathgorge Scavenger eat the graveyard their engine lives in. Then be honest about the clock: stack 003 says one alpha strike takes one seat, not three, so the moment their proximity beats every board in sight, rank them archenemy and point all five bodies at the combo seat, not the open one.

Taxes attack a deck that casts many cheap spells, and that is you — recount your hand under the tax before you plan the turn. Radagast rebates {2} on one spell per turn, which blunts the first tax and no more, and you rarely own the long game under an assembling lock: you are the beatdown here too. Name the piece that beats YOU early and break exactly that one — Boseiju from hand at instant speed, then Life from the Loam to do it again. And remember you own a stax piece yourself: Collector Ouphe switches off every mana rock at the table while 36 Forests never notice.

You are the control seat, and the traps are the whole plan. Stack 002 already wrote the sign on your lawn: attack here and everything lined up dies to a flashed Frostfang, drawing you cards on the way out. Radagast's 2/5 blocks the early turns for free, Guardian Augmenter makes him a hexproof 4/7 the moment someone tries the wall, and Saryth turns every home body hexproof besides. Let the aggro seat spend itself into the other two players, then pivot the turn you stabilise — every passive turn past stable is a free draw step for somebody else.

Fear the wrath early, welcome it late — Fecundity is the crossover card. Before your engines land, commit exactly as much board as wins before the sweeper arrives and not one body more. After Fecundity, the math flips: stack 004 verified that their Day of Judgment pays you a card per dead creature — four to you in the walked case — while Toski stands there indestructible. Bodies flashed on end steps were never exposed to a sorcery-speed wrath at all, so rebuild worst-first on their end steps and hold the finisher for their second sweeper. Your one honest gap: the 99's only wipe reads the sky, so a resolved wide ground board still has no reset here.

pilot_tips.text: Flash Hornet Queen into the flier deck's attack step — {2}{G}{G}{G} in a Radagast window buys five deathtouch blockers, and every swing after that is a losing trade for them.

departments.headline: TWO TUTORS, THREE REFUSALS
departments.dek: This deck stacked its classes and kept exactly two wishes, both creature-only. Chord of Calling refuses every one of Radagast's gifts — no discount, no Garenbrig burst, no Whisperer draw (stack 007) — and it is still the only instant-speed door to the cards redundancy cannot replace — ten walked wishes across the two of them, Whiptongue Hydra now among the fetches.

captions.Chord of Calling: **THE FINE PRINT:** Chord puts, it does not cast — so nothing that reads 'cast' fires, X must be at least 3 for Selvala, and Castle Garenbrig's six restricted green can never pay for it (stack 007).
captions.Fauna Shaman: **THE OTHER WISH:** she fetches to hand, so the card still gets cast — still discounted, still flashed, still paying the gas engines. Fetch with Chord when the timing is the point; fetch with Fauna when the cast is.

pilot_tips.text: Convoke Chord with the bodies that were not going to attack anyway — every attacker you tap to pay for it is damage off the alpha strike it fetched.

departments.headline: FORESTS ALL THE WAY DOWN
departments.dek: Thirty-six sources against a target of exactly 36, one line of pips, an 11% tap rate: the cleanest ledger this column has ever closed. The catch lives upstairs — land drops decay to 56.5% by turn six, and half the ramp package is shaped like the patch.

captions.Castle Garenbrig: **RESTRICTED FUNDS:** six green in one activation, spendable only on creature spells and creature abilities — the record settles it both ways: it pays for a flashed Craterhoof (stack 005) and never for Chord of Calling (stack 007).
captions.Forest: **THE SUPPLY:** thirty copies, enough that Wood Elves, Three Visits, Utopia Sprawl, and Castle Garenbrig's untapped clause never miss.

pilot_tips.text: Dredge Life from the Loam over a blank draw once land drops start missing — three lands back for two mana is this deck's real late-game draw spell.

departments.pull_quote: Pip share 1.00, source share 1.00. Mono-green leaves nothing to arbitrate.

departments.headline: EVERY RATE IS A FLOOR
departments.dek: The simulator never cast a single spell on an opponent's turn — no discount, no flash, no aura ramp, all three declared. It still put Radagast on the field by turn six in 94.1% of ten thousand runs. Read every figure here as the deck's worst self.

captions.Radagast of Rhosgobel: **THE CLOCK:** mean cast turn 4.0, median 4, by turn six in 94.1% of runs — the most reliable number in the file, and the one every other rate leans on.

departments.pull_quote: Mean bodies by turn six: 3.767. The bar is five. That gap is the deck's whole to-do list.

departments.headline: DOORS, NOT DEFICITS
departments.dek: Ten cards ranked for a deck the audit calls whole — zero weak axes, every breadth class answered. What is left to buy is not consistency: it is unmodeled power, led by a confirmed Game Changer that would make the whole hand castable on everyone's turn.
departments.pull_quote: Seedborn Muse moves the computed floor from 1 to exactly 3. Whether the pod reads a Muse deck as bracket 3 is the table's call, not the calculator's.
departments.note: Renderer draws the ten and their evidence bullets from considering.json. Seedborn Muse leads — a confirmed Game Changer whose pairing with Yeva, Nature's Herald makes every green creature spell castable on every turn, and whose addition moves the computed floor from 1 to exactly the target of 3. The Springheart Nantuko and Nissa, Resurgent Animist entries carry recorded-but-unwalked infinites and say so — the loop stays a candidate until a stack passes. No entry is premised on flashing a finisher (stack 005 settled that). Recon inclusion percentages describe ~800 mostly-precon first movers, not a settled meta, and the entries say that too.

departments.headline: SEVEN CASES, SEVEN HOLDINGS
departments.dek: Every step, every citation verbatim, nothing summarised. Read case A-005 first — the magazine's own favourite trick, argued in full and bounded to a wrath-dodge. A publication that files that holding against itself is one you can believe about the other six.

departments.headline: SIXTY-FIVE HANDS
departments.dek: No single painter owns this deck — the largest credit is two cards, and six artists share it. What 71 entries by 65 artists documents is thirty years of green, collected one card at a time.

featured.note:
Two cards is the biggest hand anyone holds here, and six artists hold it at once. We lead with Magali Villeneuve because her pair is the pivot in miniature: Craterhoof Behemoth, the counted kill, and Sylvan Safekeeper, the one-mana insurance that lets you commit to it. The turn this deck is built around passes through both of her paintings.

Then the honest part, said plainly: this is breadth, not curation, and we will not dress it up as taste. Fifty-nine of the 65 artists appear exactly once, the analysis flags no product runs, and a 99 assembled one printing at a time out of three decades of Magic looks precisely like this. The gallery is a survey of what green has looked like since the early sets — which is a better story than an invented favourite.

One counting note the roster insists on: Bastien Grivet painted the Forest, and you will shuffle his art thirty times a game. It counts once. Authorship is per card, not per sleeve — thirty copies is its own labelled fact, and the honest ranking stands at one entry.

also_worth_noting.note: One entry, and it is the face of the issue: Radagast of Rhosgobel himself, the portrait on the cover and atop The Command Zone.

Tied at two with a theme: Deathgorge Scavenger and Selvala, Heart of the Wilds — the 99's only graveyard answer and its only Selvala-class engine. Both of his cards are the deck's singletons of consequence.
One entry, thirty copies — the most-shuffled art in the deck. The wallpaper of every game this deck ever plays.

departments.pull_quote: One entry, thirty copies: the most-shuffled painting in the deck is still one card's worth of authorship.

departments.note: next_issue reads 'TO BE ANNOUNCED' in issue.json, so the teaser runs thin until a deck is named. Colophon carries the rules version and decklist sha 231d89ab… as standard, plus the Fan Content Policy line.

rhythm_notes: Act I front-loads identity: The Command Zone teaches at medium intensity, The Game Plan states the thesis high, and The 99 drops to browsing before Act II asks the reader to do anything. Act II climbs practice (Keep or Ship) to participation (What's Your Play?) to the peak — The Kill closes the act as the payoff, and it reads as narrative because five callout-steps walk the arithmetic as a story: the count, the night shift, the temptation, the home cast, the parachute. Act III is three consecutive Coach sections; Know Your Enemy's reference density is buffered by reflection before (Table Manners) and instruction after (Fetch Quests). Act IV's two dense analysis spreads — Sources Say and By the Numbers — sit either side of the declared full-bleed art break (BREATHER_AFTER: sources-say), and The Short List drops to imagination before the appendix. Judge's Desk's deep reference is buffered by imagination before and appreciation after (Featured Artist is this issue's gentlest spread — a 65-name breadth gallery), and the book closes low on the Back Page. No two dense sections sit adjacent anywhere outside the declared breather pair.
gaps: The Selvala same-window line — can her tapped mana pay for a flashed cast inside her own trigger window — is the frame's declared candidate line and a diagnosis open question. Until a stack passes, Fetch Quests prices her fetch as an engine for the FOLLOWING turn only, and the issue asserts nothing stronger. Highest-value next stack.

The Springheart Nantuko + Tireless Provisioner recorded infinite is unwalked, and the combo index is format-agnostic — a resolve-stack run must precede any pricing of the bracket-4 door The Short List points at. The considering entries already hedge it as 'needs a stack scenario'.

The ground board stays unanswered by design question: the 99's one wipe (Whiptongue Hydra) reads only the sky, and the diagnosis's open question names Ezuri's Predation — filed threat:tokens, invisible to the sweeper axis — as the better shape for a resolved wide ground board. Still a research-strategy call before any purchase.

The goldfish's three declared blind spots (no discount, no opponent-turn flash casts, no aura ramp) leave the binding axis — board width — genuinely unmeasured, and Yeva's lifted flash cap now widens exactly the behaviour the sim cannot see. Every width figure in the issue is labelled a floor; a sim extension modelling the discount would tell us whether the 3.767-vs-5 gap is real or an artifact.

Strategy DB holes the frame names and this issue felt: no rattlesnake/deterrence-theory section, no multiplayer flash/draw-go archetype doc, no mono-colour construction tradeoffs, and no ambush-specific child of strategy:combat-math for post-blocker flash windows.

manual_prose.matchups contains one stale card mention — 'Warg Tactics and Unforgiving Aim are still there', naming a card that is not in the 99. No furniture in this plan repeats it, and Know Your Enemy's outs exclude it, but the sentence needs a one-line scoped manual-writer fix before render.
issue.json next_issue is 'TO BE ANNOUNCED', so The Back Page closes the loop weakly until Vol. 010 is named.
